teaser.text: Workday sells organizations a shared system for managing people, money, and the administrative work between them. Its business turns that system into recurring subscriptions, then tries to deepen each customer relationship with more applications and paid use.

stock.title: Workday stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Workday's forecast spans bear, base and bull cases, shaped by paid AI, cross-selling and cash generation after stock pay.
stock.opening: Workday's weighted price reaches $238.01 by October 2029, after $172.40 in October 2027 and $203.31 in October 2028. It hinges on whether paid AI and cross-selling become cash generation after stock pay.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Workday's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Workday's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: At October 2027, the weighted price is $172.40, a 10% loss with dividends. At October 2028, it reaches $203.31, a 7% gain. At October 2029, it reaches $238.01, a 25% gain.
The October 2029 range is $76.76 to $453.56. Today’s price is $190.81, so the outcomes remain unusually wide. The bear case carries 25%. The base case carries 55%. The bull case carries 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Workday, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow after stock pay rises in the base case from $1,753 million in October 2027 to $2,068 million in October 2028. It reaches $2,320 million in October 2029. The starting point is management’s $3,180 million FY2027 free-cash-flow guide, reduced by stock pay targeted at 16% of revenue. The FY2028 outlook implies roughly $1,860 million after stock pay, with subscription revenue growth moderating to 11%. The bear case gives $1,250 million, then $1,100 million, then $1,350 million because growth slows, AI remains unpaid and restructuring absorbs cash. The bull case gives $2,050 million, then $2,600 million, then $3,150 million because paid AI, cross-selling and scale improve cash conversion.

The base case reaches $180.01 first and $232.92 last. It assumes subscription growth moderates from the guided 13% FY2027 rate toward 11% in FY2028, while renewals, backlog and customer expansion support continued cash generation. Its 55% probability is highest because it does not require rapid paid-AI adoption or a major valuation re-rating.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Workday really make?

paragraphs.text: Workday generates substantial cash, but stock pay makes conventional free cash flow more generous than the economics may feel to shareholders. Operations generated $2,939 million in FY26. Capital spending was $162 million, leaving $2,777 million of free cash flow.

earnings.opening: Workday's next results are expected on November 24, 2026. Watch for paid, repeatable AI usage as Workday reports its results.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Workday works, how it compares with rivals, who runs Workday, and what risks Workday faces.

blocks.heading: What has Workday guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: Workday’s fiscal 2027 ends in January 2027. It guides to total revenue of $10,650–$10,660 million. Subscription revenue guidance is $9,940–$9,950 million. Management expects subscription growth of 13.0% and a 31.0% non-GAAP operating margin. Fiscal 2028 guidance calls for approximately $11,000 million of subscription revenue. That represents 11.0% growth, with an adjusted operating margin of at least 33.0%. The earlier target was a 12%–15% subscription compound annual growth rate through FY28, so the new plan trades some expansion for better margins.

blocks.heading: Did Workday keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Workday also measures management through financial and customer outcomes. Fiscal 2026 bonuses funded at 101.8% of target, while customer satisfaction was 89.7%, below its target band. Management met its original subscription-revenue forecast and exceeded its adjusted-margin forecast. “Adjusted” matters because the non-GAAP measure excludes stock compensation from operating profit.

blocks.heading: What do Workday's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: July 2026 showed better operating performance, but the spectacular earnings growth was mainly a tax event. Revenue reached $2,649 million, up 12.8% year over year. Operating income rose from $248 million to $313 million. Gross margin barely moved, from 75.2% to 75.4%.

Cash moved in the opposite direction. Free cash flow fell from $588 million in July 2025 to $460 million in July 2026, partly because of payroll timing. The quarter therefore supports improving operating efficiency, not a new acceleration in sales or cash generation.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Workday's next results?

paragraphs.text: The next results must show paid, repeatable AI usage while Workday delivers its savings and preserves liquidity.
